excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.8/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#gossipsub-size-limits
> The size of the uncompressed payload must not exceed MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE or the type-specific SSZ bound, whichever is lower
this applies to all topics

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
7688 is a pure hashing change, it does not affect anything else. the limits are exactly the same than before. 
they are just _moved_ from the datatype to a runtime limit that can be freely adjusted without breaking hashing or datatypes.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: networking is _part_ of consensus. honest validators MUST implement the networking spec as specified

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: No, I don't believe that's what potuz means. "Consensus" is a very specific thing.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: maybe he means the state transition function, it's not checked in there, yes

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Like would `process_block` reject the block if something were too big.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
pre-7688 the SSZ type rejects, post-7688 the runtime limit rejects (both as a gossip rule, and inside STF), if exceeded.
the 10 MB MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE is only enforced on the network level, not in the STF

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: with heze they have these weird rules for the inclusion list where one has to serialize just the transactions part and look at its serialized length (8 KB), that's the only case where I think that the length of _serialized_ data (instead of actual content length) is checked.

excerpts.author: wemeetagain
excerpts.content: I suppose the consensus concern is that if a codepath exists to feed size-unchecked data into a chain, you can create a chain split. Whereas pre-7688, sizing was implicitly part of STF bc no size-unchecked data can be represented.

excerpts.author: wemeetagain
excerpts.content: In practice, there's only 3 codepaths to ingest chain data: gossip, reqresp, and api. So if we have size checks on all three it should be fine?

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: it's only a chain split if it is possible to create a valid message for that size

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: for API there's data from REST (VC / public API publishing blocks through that), and from the engine (kinda trusted, but also historically buggy so CL in practice still wants to validate)

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: there's also the mechanism where a tiny payload can blow up the beaconblock with deposits by deploying a contract that spends all ETH into the deposit contract, and just sending it a couple thousand ETH without any calldata. where the beaconblock exceeds the 10 MB

excerpts.content: essentially, staking pool contract
